name: stem-workbench
description: Non-commercial Electron desktop product for stem-splitter-live: six live stems from a YouTube view or a local file. Pre-alpha — the app runs from a checkout; no installer has ever been built or signed.

buildNotes._: PROSE FOR `build`, KEPT OUT OF IT. electron-builder validates its configuration against a schema and refuses unknown properties, so a `_` comment inside `build` would be a config that cannot run — which is the one thing a block labelled CONFIGURED must not be. npm ignores unknown top-level keys, so it lives here instead.
buildNotes.status: WRITTEN, THEN BUILT ON LINUX FOR THE FIRST TIME. `npm run dist:linux` produced dist/stem-workbench-0.0.0.AppImage (197 MB) and dist/stem-workbench_0.0.0_amd64.deb on this box, and `tools/suites/dist-linux.mjs` builds one and LAUNCHES it, asserting the app's own `[main] ready` line. macOS AND WINDOWS ARE STILL CONFIGURATION AND NOT EVIDENCE: no dmg, no zip and no exe has been produced on any machine, and nothing has been signed or notarized. README.md 'What was verified, and what was only configured'.
buildNotes.extraResources: THE 109 MB OF WEIGHTS GO ON DISK, NOT INSIDE THE ASAR. HOST-DESIGN.md 7.1 chose this over asarUnpack: both put a plain file on disk, but asarUnpack's path is derived by string surgery on app.getAppPath(), and process.resourcesPath is documented and the same shape on all three platforms. src/main/main.js's MODEL_DIR reads exactly this location when app.isPackaged. The unit re-verifies the SHA-256 and the byte count on every load over whatever the Host hands it (rule M1), so a truncated or substituted copy is refused at load rather than trusted because it came out of our own installer.
buildNotes.mac: NOTARIZATION IS CONFIGURED AND HAS NEVER RUN. It needs an Apple Developer ID, an app-specific password and a Mac; this repository has none of the three. `notarize` is left true so that a build on a machine that HAS them does the right thing, and one that does not fails loudly instead of shipping an unnotarized dmg that Gatekeeper will refuse on the user's machine.
buildNotes.win: UNSIGNED DURING BETA, ON PURPOSE — seed §14: testers click through SmartScreen. Azure Trusted Signing is CONFIGURED IN `dist:win:signed` AND NOWHERE ELSE, and that is deliberate: app-builder-lib/out/winPackager.js:35 switches to the Azure signer the moment `win.azureSignOptions` exists, and its `initialize()` runs PowerShell `Install-Module TrustedSigning` unconditionally — so a block sitting in `build.win` would break every unsigned beta build. Putting it on a script instead leaves `npm run dist:win` producing the unsigned exe the decision asks for, while the four fields and the three Entra environment variables are committed, greppable and asserted by tools/suites/updates.mjs.
buildNotes.linux: THE ONE PLATFORM ANYTHING HAS ACTUALLY RUN ON — and now as an artifact, not only as `npm start`. `maintainer` is REQUIRED for the deb: without it (or a top-level `author` with an email) app-builder-lib/out/targets/FpmTarget.ts:126 fails the build, which is how the first Linux build on this box ended — the AppImage was written and the deb was not. `syncDesktopName` is the other half: without it electron-builder warned that the installed .desktop filename does not match Electron's app_id / StartupWMClass, so a desktop environment does not link the running window to its launcher entry. `desktopName` itself is NOT set — it is a TOP-LEVEL package.json key, not a `build.linux` one (the schema rejects it there), and with `syncDesktopName` it falls back to `executableName`, which is already `stem-workbench`.
buildNotes.publish: `publish` NAMES THE FEED AND `--publish never` IS ON EVERY SCRIPT. Those are two different things and the standing ruling only forbids the second: electron-builder writes `publish` into `app-update.yml` inside the installer, which is WHERE THE UPDATER READS ITS FEED FROM — an installer built with `publish: null` can never update itself no matter what the app does. `--publish never` is what stops a build from CREATING a GitHub Release, and it stays on `dist`, `dist:dir`, `dist:mac`, `dist:win`, `dist:win:signed` and `dist:linux`. `releaseType: prerelease` is the beta channel, seed §14; `src/main/update.js`'s UPDATER_FEED carries the same object and `tools/suites/updates.mjs` compares the two both ways.
buildNotes.updater: electron-updater IS CONFIGURED AND IS NOT A DEPENDENCY OF THIS APP, and that is a measured decision rather than an omission. Read against electron-updater@6.8.9: out/electronHttpExecutor.js:7 makes its own `session.fromPartition("electron-updater")`, which is a session outside src/main/sessions.js and therefore outside the P1' observer; out/providers/GitHubProvider.js:32,43 talks to `github.com`, not the `api.github.com` that UPDATE_HOST names, so `mayRequest()` cancels every request it makes; and a release asset redirects to `objects.githubusercontent.com`, so the download path is irreducibly two hosts. P1' names ONE. Since this project also never creates a GitHub Release, arming it would buy an unobserved session and three hosts in exchange for a download that cannot happen. docs/UPDATES.md states exactly what would have to change first.
buildNotes.nativeBackend: THE CoreML BACKEND IS CONFIGURED HERE AND HAS NEVER BEEN BUILT, RUN OR TIMED BY ANYBODY. Seed §16's native inference backend runs in an Electron utility process (`src/utility/inference.js`) over `onnxruntime-node` with the CoreML execution provider, and `src/main/backend.js`'s `nativeIsPossible()` scopes it to darwin/arm64 — Apple Silicon only, because that is where the Neural Engine is; CoreML on an Intel Mac is CPU/GPU and a different claim. THAT PACKAGE IS DELIBERATELY NOT A DEPENDENCY OF THIS PROJECT AND MUST NOT BE ADDED CASUALLY: it is a native module, every worktree on the build box shares one `node_modules`, and WORKTREES.md §2.4 forbids `npm install` inside a worktree because a tool that rewrites one file in place corrupts the main checkout for every other agent. Adding it is an owner action in the main checkout followed by a re-seed of every worktree. Until then `src/utility/inference.js` requires it inside a try/catch, its absence is the ordinary answer `no-module`, and `src/main/backend.js`'s selection returns the ORT worker — which on Linux it does anyway, one gate above, because the platform gate sits above the probe.
buildNotes.asarUnpack: A NATIVE `.node` BINARY CANNOT BE LOADED FROM INSIDE AN ASAR ARCHIVE, so the moment `onnxruntime-node` becomes a dependency it has to be unpacked or every macOS build fails at the first `require` in the utility process. The glob is written NOW, while it matches nothing and cannot break a build, so that whoever adds the dependency does not also have to discover this. It is the counterpart of `extraResources` above rather than a contradiction of it: the weights are DATA and go beside the asar by a documented path; this is EXECUTABLE CODE that has to sit on a real filesystem for dlopen to reach it. macOS is also where the hardened runtime meets an unsigned third-party dylib — `build/entitlements.mac.plist` already carries `com.apple.security.cs.disable-library-validation`, which that plist documents as Electron's own requirement and which is ALSO exactly what an `onnxruntime-node` `.node` needs. Do not tidy it away as Electron-only.
buildNotes.nativeBackendNeverBuilt: WHAT NOBODY HERE CAN ANSWER ABOUT THE TWO NOTES ABOVE. Measured on the build box rather than assumed, so that the first person to build this knows where to look instead of trusting a green. (1) THIS PROJECT HAS NO PRODUCTION DEPENDENCIES AT ALL: there is no `dependencies` key in this file, only `devDependencies`, and `files` below is an explicit ALLOWLIST that names no `node_modules` pattern. electron-builder documents that production dependencies are copied regardless of `files`, but that behaviour has never been exercised on this repository because there has never been one to copy — `onnxruntime-node` would be the first. If it is NOT packed, `asarUnpack` unpacks a directory that was never packed and the app degrades SILENTLY to `no-module` and the ORT worker at runtime instead of failing loudly at build time. Check the packaged tree for `app.asar.unpacked/node_modules/onnxruntime-node` before believing a build succeeded. (2) ELECTRON-BUILDER IS NOT INSTALLED IN THIS CHECKOUT. It is declared in `devDependencies` and `node_modules` holds only `electron` and `playwright-core`, so `npm run dist` cannot run here and NOTHING HAS EVER PARSED THIS `build` BLOCK — the schema validation the `_` note above relies on has never once been applied to it. `.github/workflows/package.yml` running `npm ci` on `macos-14` is the only place it could be, and that workflow is dispatch- and tag-triggered, so it has not run either. (3) THE TWO MAC ARCHITECTURES ARE SEPARATE DOWNLOADS. `mac.target` builds arm64 AND x64, `nativeIsPossible()` answers true only on arm64, and a dual-arch dmg therefore needs per-arch `npmRebuild` that nobody here can test. The x64 half is not broken by this — it takes the ORT worker, the same path Linux takes — but it is not the claim seed §16 makes either. See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §5b and docs/TESTING.md §5g.

linux.synopsis: Six live stems from a YouTube view or a local file, on-device
linux.description: stem-workbench separates audio into six stems on your own machine, from a YouTube view it embeds or from a local file. The model runs on-device; nothing is uploaded. Non-commercial: the bundled htdemucs_6s weights are CC BY-NC 4.0 (NOTICE.md).
